mappings.note: Four parts: respiratory-system labels and the pathway (C 3.2-LO-2); how lungs maximise exchange area, which is the alveolus (C 4.2-LO-1); factors setting the direction of diffusion in plants and why aquatic animals breathe faster, both non-human (C 3.2). Three codes because the row is really three questions.
Heart diagram: the chamber collecting oxygenated blood, the largest vessel, the septum, the vessel to the lungs. Human circulation, C 3.2-LO-2.
Guard cells regulating the pore is turgor at the cell level (C 3.1); what happens to the rate of photosynthesis when dust blocks the stomata is autotrophic nutrition (C 3.2-LO-1).
Salivary amylase, emulsification and the substrate of respiration are nutrition (C 3.2-LO-1); why lungs are divided into tiny sacs is the alveolus surface-area argument (C 4.2-LO-1).
Labelling the organ that makes urine and the one that releases it is C 3.2-LO-2; the end products of fat and protein digestion is C 3.2-LO-1.
Human excretory labels and how urine is produced are C 3.2-LO-2; two excretory products of PLANTS falls outside that human-only outcome, so the competency C 3.2 is cited for it.

Amoeba's pseudopodia and their second use, the glands that digest starch, and how stomach and intestinal pH are maintained. All nutrition, C 3.2-LO-1; the pH part is a digestive condition, not a C 1.3 acid-base question.
Labelled heart diagram and the function of two chambers -- C 3.2-LO-2.

The nephron diagram with Bowman's capsule, glomerulus and collecting duct, plus the function of the kidney's structural unit, is C 4.2-LO-1; the artificial-kidney function is the excretory pathway more broadly, C 3.2-LO-2.
Respiratory-system labels (C 3.2-LO-2) bolted to a request for two parasitic plants and two parasitic animals (C 3.2-LO-1). Unrelated halves in one row.
Experiment proving sunlight is necessary for photosynthesis -- autotrophic nutrition plus the partial-covering controlled variable, C 8.1.

Three distinct parts: the fate of glucose, amino acids, salts and water in the nephron (C 3.2-LO-2); a labelled stomata diagram with functions (C 3.1); and the raw materials and equation of photosynthesis (C 3.2-LO-1).
Five functions of blood -- the transport medium in C 3.2-LO-2.
Heart labels by function, the composition of blood, and the role of haemoglobin. All human transport, C 3.2-LO-2.
Alimentary-canal labels by function, the role of stomach HCl, and what the gastric and anal sphincters do. Human digestion throughout, C 3.2-LO-1.
Respiratory-system labels are the pathway (C 3.2-LO-2); 'what are alveoli and their role in respiration' is the alveolus structure-function outcome (C 4.2-LO-1).

Four parts. O2/CO2 transport in the human body is C 3.2-LO-2; water movement during transpiration and food transport in plants are C 4.3-LO-1; the closing argument that diffusion cannot supply leaves and roots is the body-organisation point, C 4.2.

Single circulation in fish, the respiratory pigment and where it sits, and why heart and veins have valves. All circulation; C 3.2-LO-2 even though the fish part is non-human, because the item is anchored on the human heart.
Mechanism of blood circulation and the role of lymph -- both components of human transport, C 3.2-LO-2.
The human excretory system is C 3.2-LO-2; four strategies plants use for excretion sits outside that human-only outcome, so C 3.2 is cited for the second half.
The finger-like projections of the small intestine are the villi, C 4.2-LO-1's named structure; the use of residual lung volume is the respiratory pathway, C 3.2-LO-2.
Heart section identified by function: the chamber pumping deoxygenated blood, the vessel taking oxygenated blood away, the vein from the lower body. C 3.2-LO-2.
Respiratory-system labels and the advantage of residual volume in the breathing cycle -- C 3.2-LO-2.
Heart section labels and why ventricles are thicker than atria -- C 3.2-LO-2.
Heart section: the septum preventing mixing, the valves preventing backflow, and the receiving and pumping chambers. C 3.2-LO-2.

DEFECT: the stem has swallowed answer text -- it ends '...Part which stores the Purpose. To collect excretory products for expulsion from body.' The intended item labels the respiratory and excretory systems, both C 3.2-LO-2.
Nutrition in Amoeba and in Paramoecium, plus the storage forms of unused carbohydrate and of food energy. All nutrition, C 3.2-LO-1.
Nutrition modes of fungi and Cuscuta, the parts of the alimentary canal by function, and two gastric secretions with their roles. Entirely C 3.2-LO-1.
Major steps of urine formation and how breathing is brought about -- excretion and respiration pathways in humans, both C 3.2-LO-2.
Transpiration vs translocation and why plant transport is slow are C 4.3-LO-1; what stomata are and how they open and close is guard-cell turgor, C 3.1.
Excretory-system diagram plus the functions of renal artery, kidney, ureter and bladder -- naming the organs of human excretion, C 3.2-LO-2.
What lymph is, how it differs from plasma, its direction of flow and two functions -- a component of the human transport system, C 3.2-LO-2.
Respiratory diagram labelled by function: cartilage-ringed organ, gas-exchange structure, voice box, flattening muscle. The pathway and its organs, C 3.2-LO-2.
Why bile matters despite having no enzyme, and the products of complete digestion. C 3.2-LO-1.
Respiratory diagram plus reasons for residual volume and mucus-lined nostrils -- C 3.2-LO-2.
Labelled heart with its major vessels, and what selective reabsorption is. Circulation and excretion, both inside C 3.2-LO-2.
A labelled nephron (C 4.2-LO-1's named structure) bolted to an aerobic-vs-anaerobic respiration comparison (C 3.2-LO-3). Two unrelated halves.
Protein digestion in stomach and small intestine is C 3.2-LO-1; how the small intestine is designed to absorb is the villus structure-function outcome C 4.2-LO-1.
What stomata are and what they do (exchange of materials, C 3.2); how they open and close (guard-cell turgor, C 3.1). Same split as qid:85772.
Heart section with right ventricle and septum, the artery carrying deoxygenated blood, the chamber receiving oxygenated blood, and why ventricle walls are thicker. C 3.2-LO-2.
Location and function of the four major digestive glands -- C 3.2-LO-1.
Heart section labels and what the pulmonary vein and vena cava carry are C 3.2-LO-2; what xylem and phloem carry is C 4.3-LO-1. The item deliberately sets plant transport beside animal transport.
Excretory-system labels including aorta and vena cava, plus two vital kidney functions. Human excretion and its blood supply, C 3.2-LO-2.
Labelling a schematic of O2/CO2 transport through the heart and distinguishing pulmonary artery from pulmonary vein. C 3.2-LO-2.

Three parts: wilting leaves point to a blocked xylem (C 4.3-LO-1); stomatal opening and closing is guard-cell turgor (C 3.1); the physical phenomenon of gas exchange between plant and air is diffusion (C 3.2).
Near-duplicate of qid:85868 -- heart labels with what xylem, phloem, pulmonary vein and vena cava transport. Mapped to the same pair so the duplicates stay consistent.
Gas exchange across stem, root and leaf surfaces is exchange of materials in a plant (C 3.2, since LO-2 is human-only); how water and minerals are transported is C 4.3-LO-1.
How water rises in a tall tree without a pump, and three xylem-vs-phloem differences. Both halves are C 4.3-LO-1, the last of the 10SCIENCE6qa run.
